scope: Also covers category-level pose and size estimation of unseen instances within known object categories, its canonical-coordinate representations such as NOCS, and training losses that make pose regression tolerant to object symmetry.

concepts.title: Category-level object pose estimation
concepts.definition: Estimating the 6D pose, and usually the 3D size, of previously unseen object instances that belong to categories known at training time, without an exact CAD model of each instance.

evidence.phrase: the first category-level pose estimation approach
category-level pose techniques for opaque objects
category-level pose estimation for transparent objects

near_pairs.name: Novel-object 6D pose estimation
near_pairs.why: Both estimate poses of objects unseen in training; category-level needs the category at training time and no CAD model, novel-object needs a CAD model or reference images at test time (^labbe2022megapose-003 contrasts them).

concepts.title: Normalized Object Coordinate Space
concepts.definition: A canonical unit-cube coordinate frame in which all instances of a category are consistently oriented and scaled, so that a network can predict per-pixel canonical coordinates (a NOCS map) and recover pose and size by aligning them with observed depth.

relations.quote: NOCS estimates category-level 6D pose from RGB-D images by transforming every object pixel to a shared coordinate frame

concepts.title: Symmetry-aware pose loss
concepts.definition: A pose training loss that does not penalise predictions equivalent under an object's symmetry, either by taking the minimum over the symmetric ground-truth poses or by matching each predicted model point to the closest ground-truth point.

evidence.phrase: loss functions for specific symmetry types

near_pairs.name: ShapeMatch-Loss (SLOSS)
near_pairs.why: PoseCNN's closest-point loss is one instance of the general idea; kept inside this concept rather than as its own note.

near_pairs.name: ADD and ADD-S metrics
near_pairs.why: ADD-S applies the same closest-point matching as ShapeMatch-Loss, but as an evaluation metric rather than a training loss.
